parameters.subject: Weekly Treatment Recovery Summary — Willow Creek Dental

parameters.content:
## 🤖 Dental Treatment Recovery

Finds treatment plans a dentist diagnosed but that never got booked, automatically follows up with the patient by email on a set cadence, and hands anything that goes cold to a human instead of nagging forever.

### 🧩 Why This Isn't Just Another Reminder Bot
- Most "reminder" workflows just resend the same message forever — this one escalates to a human instead of repeating itself endlessly on high-value plans
- Nothing patient-facing ever contains a diagnosis or procedure name — the message stays deliberately generic
- Built against Open Dental's actual field names (ProcCode, ProcStatus, PlannedAptNum) so a demo Google Sheet can be swapped for the live API with zero restructuring
- Two independent schedules (daily follow-ups, weekly owner report) share one source of truth instead of duplicating logic
- A $3,000 crown and a $200 filling don't get chased the same way — escalation weighs both time waiting and dollar value

### 🔍 What It Does
This workflow:
- Checks a spreadsheet (or Open Dental) every day for treatment plans that were diagnosed but never scheduled
- Works out which patients are overdue for their next nudge based on how long it's been sitting
- Sends the next reminder email in a 3-step sequence (gentle, firmer, final)
- Flags anything that's gone quiet for too long so staff make a personal phone call instead
- Updates the sheet after every action so tomorrow's run knows exactly where things stand
- Sends a weekly email to the practice owner showing how much money got recovered

### ⚙️ How It Works
- Two Schedule Triggers run independently: a daily follow-up check and a weekly summary
- Google Sheets nodes pull the Patients and ProcedureLog tabs fresh on every run — no cached state
- A Code node (Decide Follow-Up Action) cross-references FollowUpStage and DaysUnscheduled against a fixed cadence (3 / 14 / 30 / 45 days) to output one action per row
- An IF node splits rows into "escalate to staff" vs "send next email" based on that decision
- Gmail nodes send either a generic patient reminder or a detailed internal alert
- Google Sheets Update nodes write the new stage and contact date back so state persists between runs
- The weekly branch recomputes its own totals directly from ProcedureLog rather than trusting stored summary formulas, so the report can't drift out of sync

### 💪 Key Capabilities
- Self-contained state machine — no external database, the spreadsheet is the whole memory
- Dollar-value-aware escalation instead of one-size-fits-all reminders
- Deliberately privacy-conscious patient messaging (no diagnosis or procedure details in emails)
- Field-for-field compatible with the Open Dental API for a same-day swap from demo to production
- Two schedules, one data model — no duplicate logic to maintain

### 📦 Requirements
- A Google Sheet with Patients and ProcedureLog tabs (column structure documented in the sheet's own ReadMe tab)
- Google Sheets OAuth2 credential
- Gmail OAuth2 credential
- For production use with real patient data: an Open Dental API developer key + customer key, and a signed BAA (this handles PHI — see HIPAA notes before connecting a real practice)

### 💡 Example Use Cases
- Dental, orthodontic, or specialty practices with a backlog of diagnosed-but-unbooked treatment
- Any practice management workflow where "diagnosed" and "actually happened" quietly drift apart
- Practice owners who want a standing dollar-recovered number instead of guessing at lost revenue
- Front desk teams too busy to manually track who's overdue for a callback

## Step 1: Pull today's data

Every morning, this grabs the full patient list and the full list of diagnosed treatments from the spreadsheet — fresh, not cached — so everything downstream works off today's real numbers.

## Step 2: Decide what each patient needs

For every treatment that's still unscheduled, this works out how many days it's been waiting and what's already been tried, then decides: send the next email, or hand it to a human instead.

## Step 3a: Hand cold leads to staff

If a plan has gone quiet after three emails, nobody gets a fourth automated message. The front desk gets an email with the patient's name, phone number, and value — and the sheet is marked so it stops nagging on its own.

## Step 3b: Send the next reminder

For everyone else, this sends the next email in the sequence — first gentle, then firmer — using only generic wording, then records in the sheet which email just went out and when.

## Step 4 (runs weekly): Report the wins to the owner

On a separate schedule, this adds up how much treatment got booked or completed this week, how much is still sitting unscheduled, and emails a plain summary to the practice owner.
